extracted.intended_audience: publishers, editors, research integrity professionals, librarians, platform providers, and others involved in scholarly peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Developing, harmonizing, and publishing a standardized taxonomy and terminology for peer review processes (initially for journal articles) to increase clarity, transparency, and consistent communication across the scholarly ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is the process of evaluating academic, scientific, or professional work; it is used by academic journals to support research integrity by filtering out invalid or poor-quality articles, and to ensure research outcomes are exposed to relevant audiences through publication in relevant journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes dual functions: quality control (filtering invalid/poor work) and dissemination (ensuring exposure to relevant audiences). Use this purpose as the foundation when describing or assessing peer review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and consistent nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Many new peer review models have been introduced without an accompanying clear and consistent nomenclature, leading to confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards should provide unambiguous, harmonized terminology so different stakeholders (authors, reviewers, editors, readers) can understand and compare review models and practices without ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: There is increased support for more openness and transparency in science and research, including peer review, in order to maintain trust in the scholarly ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology and taxonomy should support and enable transparent and open peer review practices (e.g., by making review models and disclosure practices explicit), thereby contributing to trust in scholarly communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonizing and communicating definitions of discrete elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop standard definitions and best practice recommendations for the communication of peer review processes so community members—whether authors, reviewers, editors or readers—can quickly and easily recognize how to more productively participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards should define discrete elements of peer review (roles, actions, status labels, model types) and include best-practice guidance for communicating those elements to stakeholders to enable consistent interpretation and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and extensibility of the taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Initially the taxonomy is designed for peer review of journal articles, but the intention is to expand to other outputs in future (e.g., books), based on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the terminology/taxonomy with a clear initial scope (journal articles) while ensuring extensibility so it can be adapted to other scholarly outputs as needs arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards development and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: NISO is taking STM's output and developing it into a version 3.0, which will be made available for public comment and then published as a formal ANSI/NISO standard once it has been reviewed and approved by NISO Voting Members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow an open development process: consolidate community input, publish for public comment, and obtain formal approval through organizational voting to ensure legitimacy and broad buy-in for the terminology standard.
